overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the unlisted agreement was not "used" at the meeting, and the draft minutes' lack of detail was cured when the approved final minutes were adopted.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the July 1 meeting allegedly failed to list all documents used, specifically the Administrative Services Agreement.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore conclude that the ASA was not "used" during the meeting for the purposes of the Open Meeting Law, thus CVEC did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to list the ASA in its minutes.

allegations.summary: Draft minutes of the July 1 meeting allegedly lacked sufficient detail on deliberations, such as vague descriptions of committee review and O&M discussion.
allegations.key_passage: However, because the minutes were merely in draft form, and CVEC still had the opportunity to (and actually did) revise them, we find that there was no Open Meeting Law violation.
